findings.description: Removing the land's signal listener means a terminal Ctrl-C now kills node itself mid-`execFileSync`. `withMergeLock`'s `finally` never runs, the `.git` merge lock stays behind, and every later `pup merge`/`pup land` refuses. The new comment says the opposite will happen.

The moved comment "The gate's teardown usually removed both already; the land then has nothing to do there." now sits above the locked-worktree test, where nothing was removed. It describes 'lands a session whose worktree and branch are already gone' (line 655) and should sit above that test.

Decision 84 says the row's id, worktree and branch are "compared as text", but `src/core/land.service.ts:84` now compares the worktree with `join(req.repoPath, '.worktrees', session.id)`. `join` normalizes the path, so the comparison is no longer pure text. Reword the clause to match the code comment: the id's shape is checked first, then the worktree is compared against the joined path.

`tearDown` now returns `{removedWorktree: false, keptWorktree, keptBranch}` early and the normal path returns `{removedWorktree, keptBranch?}`. The CLI's `else if` relies on an invariant the type doesn't carry: `keptWorktree` implies `keptBranch`. Document that coupling on `LandOutcome`, or drop `keptBranch` from the early return and let the kept-worktree message cover the branch.

AGENTS.md says "`src/cli/` stays thin; logic lives in `src/core/`". Inlining `withLockReleasedOnSignal` puts the lock-path computation, the `heldOnEntry` check, the lock `rmSync` and the signal registration directly in the `pup merge` action body. Signal handling is CLI-owned, so this is arguable, but a CLI-local helper would keep the action body thin.

process_issues.description: Correctness, security and maintainability each ran as one instance. The delta's 10 files span src and docs, which technically meets the >8-files/2-areas scaling gate. I didn't scale them because the delta is only about 295 changed lines, docs/ is a single file, and 44 of the lines are tests. review-context was not spawned because the delta touches no CORS/HTTP/docker/CI/settings surface.

The validator confirmed the important signal-handling finding but corrected one sub-claim: `pup ui`'s `q` sends SIGTERM only to the merge child (use-controls.hook.ts L341), never to `pup land`. I removed the SIGTERM point from the posted body.
